Rashi on Eruvin 82b:13:1.hebrew: מתכוונין להקל - ר' מאיר סבר: בשבת אכיל איניש טפי, משום דבסים תבשיליה, ואמרי אינשי: "רווחא לבסימא שכיח". ור' יהודה סבר: כיון דבשבת סועד שלש סעודות, אינו אוכל הרבה בכל סעודה:
Rashi on Eruvin 82b:13:1.english: [Both] intended to be lenient - Rabbi Meir holds: On Shabbat, a person eats more because his food is delicious, and people say: "Room is [always] found for delicious [food]." And Rabbi Yehuda holds: Since on Shabbat one eats three meals, he does not eat much at each meal.

Rashi on Eruvin 82b:14:1.hebrew: ככר הלקוח מן הנחתום בפונדיון כשנמכרים ארבע סאין בסלע - השתא ס"ד, חצי קב הוי שתי סעודות. כיצד? ו' מעות לדינר, מעה — שתי פונדיונין, נמצא דינר — י"ב פונדיונין, נמצא סלע — מ"ח פונדיונין. וסאה — ו' קבין, לד' סאין — כ"ד קבין; הרי מ"ח חצאי קבין — חצי קב לפונדיון:
Rashi on Eruvin 82b:14:1.english: A loaf purchased from the baker for a pundeyon when four se’a are sold for a sela - Now it enters our mind [that] half a kav is two meals. How so? Six ma’ot to a dinar; a ma’ah [is] two pundeyonim; it turns out [that] a dinar is twelve pundeyonim; it turns out [that] a sela is forty-eight pundeyonim. And a se’ah [is] six kavim; for four se’a, [there are] twenty-four kavim; behold, [there are] forty-eight half-kavim — half a kav per pundeyon.

Rashi on Eruvin 82b:14:2.hebrew: ר"ש - ממעט משיעור, ואומר: תשע סעודות יש לקב, ודי לעירוב בב' ידות של ככר של ג' ככרות לקב. נמצאת ככר השלימה שלישית הקב, וב' ידותיה הוו שתי סעודות:
Rashi on Eruvin 82b:14:2.english: Rabbi Shimon - [He] reduces the measure and says: There are nine meals to a kav, and it is sufficient for an eruv [to consist of] two parts of a loaf of three loaves to a kav. The complete loaf thus turns out to be one-third of a kav, and its two parts are two meals.

Rashi on Eruvin 82b:15:1.hebrew: חציה לבית המנוגע - סתמא היא, והכי קאמר: חצי ככר השלימה ששיערו בה את העירוב — ובין למר ובין למר — לשהיית בית המנוגע לטמא בגדים. הנכנס טמא מיד, דכתיב: (ויקרא י״ד:מ״ו) והבא אל הבית יטמא; אבל כבוס בגדים לא נאמרה בו עד שישהה כדי אכילה, דכתיב: (שם) והאוכל בבית יכבס את בגדיו, ומוקמינן לה בתורת כהנים לשוהה כדי סעודה, ואע"פ שלא אכל. וחצי ככר זו הוי כדי אכילה; אע"ג דלר"ש לענין עירובין הוי בככר ג' סעודות — התם הוא דבשיעור העירוב נתכוונו כולן להקל, אבל שיעור סעודה קים להו לרבנן הכי, ובעינן שישהה בכדי אכילת חצי ככר זו. והוא פרס דכוליה הש"ס, על שם ששיעורה בפרוסה, כלומר: בחצי ככר:
Rashi on Eruvin 82b:15:1.english: Half of it for a leprous house - This is an anonymous [statement], and this is what it means: Half of the complete loaf with which they measured the eruv — and whether according to this Master or according to that Master — [is the measure of time] for remaining in a leprous house to defile garments. One who enters becomes impure immediately, as it is written: (Leviticus 14:46) "And he that goeth into the house... shall be unclean"; however, laundering of garments was not stated concerning him until he remains for the duration of eating [a meal], as it is written: (ibid. 14:47) "And he that eateth in the house shall wash his clothes," and we establish this in Torat Kohanim as [referring to] one who remains for the duration of a meal, even though he did not eat. And half of this loaf is [the duration of] "the time of eating." Even though according to Rabbi Shimon, regarding eruvin there are three meals in a loaf — it is there, regarding the measure of the eruv, that they all intended to be lenient; but as for the measure of a meal, the Rabbis established it as such, and we require that he remain for the duration of eating half of this loaf. And this is the peras [mentioned] throughout the entire Talmud, so named because its measure is a piece [perusa], that is to say, half a loaf.

Rashi on Eruvin 82b:15:2.hebrew: לפסול את הגוייה - האוכל אוכלין טמאין כחצי פרס, נפסלה גוייתו מלאכול בתרומה. ומדרבנן הוא, דאין אוכל מטמא אדם, ורבנן גזרו שהאוכלו יפסל בתרומה עד שיטבול, כדאמר בפרק בתרא דיומא (דף פ:): הנח לטומאת גוייה, דלאו דאורייתא:
Rashi on Eruvin 82b:15:2.english: To disqualify the body - One who eats ritually impure food [in the amount of] half a peras, his body is disqualified from eating teruma. And it is [only] by rabbinic decree, for food does not impart ritual impurity to a person [by Torah law], and the Rabbis decreed that one who eats it is disqualified from [eating] teruma until he immerses [in a ritual bath], as [the Gemara] says in the final chapter of Yoma (80b): "Leave aside the impurity of the body, which is not of Torah law."

Rashi on Eruvin 82b:16:1.hebrew: וכמה - לר"מ ולר' יהודה קבעי:
Rashi on Eruvin 82b:16:1.english: And how much - [The Gemara] is asking according to Rabbi Meir and according to Rabbi Yehuda.

Rashi on Eruvin 82b:16:2.hebrew: ריפתא איכרייתא - שנושאין האכרים עמהם לשדה. אכרים — מנהיגי שוורים:
Rashi on Eruvin 82b:16:2.english: Farmers' loaves - [Loaves] that the farmers carry with them to the field. "Farmers" [means] drivers of oxen.

Rashi on Eruvin 82b:16:3.english: Nehar Papita - It is a place [called] Nehar Pappa.

Rashi on Eruvin 82b:17:1.hebrew: אבוך כמאן - מהנך תנאי סבירא ליה בעירוב: כר' יהודה או כר' מאיר? דקי"ל בעירוב: לכל אדם כדי מזונו, ואם בא לשער בעצמו — באיזו ישער: בשבת או בחול:
Rashi on Eruvin 82b:17:1.english: Your father, in accordance with whose [opinion] - Which of these tanna'im does he hold in accordance with regarding an eiruv: like Rabbi Yehuda or like Rabbi Meir? For we establish that regarding an eiruv, for each person [the measure is] according to his [own] sustenance; and if he comes to measure for himself, by which [standard] should he measure: on Shabbat or on a weekday?

Rashi on Eruvin 82b:17:2.hebrew: דאי כר' יהודה קשיא לי הא דאמרי אינשי רווחא לבסימא שכיח - כלומר, המעיים מתרווחין לפנות מקום לדבר המתוק:
Rashi on Eruvin 82b:17:2.english: For if [it were] in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, that which people say, "Room is found for a sweet [food]," would be difficult for me - That is to say, the intestines expand to make room for something sweet.

Rashi on Eruvin 82b:18:1.english: Their statements - [Those] of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka and Rabbi Shimon.

Rashi on Eruvin 82b:19:1.hebrew: צא מהן שליש לחנוני - רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה לא הזכיר חצי קב, ששיער לך אלא בככר הלקוח מן החנוני בפונדיון. והרי החנוני משתכר בחצי קב שלקח בפונדיון שליש, ומוכר ב' שלישי חצי קב בפונדיון, ובהך שני שלישי אשמעינן רבי יוחנן דאיכא שתי סעודות — הרי בחצי קב שלש סעודות:
Rashi on Eruvin 82b:19:1.english: Deduct from them one-third for the shopkeeper - Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka did not mention half a kav; for he evaluated for you only [the measure of] a loaf bought from the shopkeeper for a pundeyon. And behold, the shopkeeper earns a profit of one-third on the half-kav that he bought for a pundeyon, and sells two-thirds of a half-kav for a pundeyon, and regarding these two-thirds, Rabbi Yoḥanan teaches us that there are two meals — thus, in a half-kav, there are three meals.

Rashi on Eruvin 82b:1:1.hebrew: אמר רב יהושע - ודאי כדאמרת, בן ה' אינו יוצא עד שיערבו עליו, ורב אסי נמי בשעירבה אמו עליו קאמר. וקמ"ל, דאם עירב עליו אביו לרוח אחרת — בתר אמו שדינן ליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 82b:1:1.english: Rav Yehoshua said - Certainly [it is] as you said: a child of five does not go out unless they establish an eiruv for him, and Rav Asi also spoke of [a case] where his mother established an eiruv for him. And it teaches us that if his father established an eiruv for him in another direction, we cast him after his mother.

Rashi on Eruvin 82b:23:1.hebrew: ציבי - עצים לאפות — אין החנוני משתכר אלא שליש:
Rashi on Eruvin 82b:23:1.english: Wood - Wood for baking — [in that case,] the grocer profits only one-third.

Rashi on Eruvin 82b:2:1.hebrew: מיתיבי כו' עד בן שש - הא ליכא למימר בשערב עליו זה לכאן וזה לכאן, דהא "עד" קתני, דמשמע: בן שנה ובן שתים ושלש, עד בן שש — יוצא בעירוב אמו. וכי היכי דבן שנה ובן שתים בלא זיכוי עירוב קאמר, בן ד' ובן ה' נמי בלא עירבו עליו קאמר. וכי נמי אמרינן "עד ולא עד בכלל", הויא תיובתא דרב יהושע, דתריץ דבן ה' צריך לזכות לו. תיובתא:
Rashi on Eruvin 82b:2:1.english: They raised an objection... up to the age of six - Here, it cannot be said [that it is dealing with a case] where [each parent] established an eiruv on his behalf, one in this direction and one in that direction, for it teaches "until," which implies: a one-year-old, a two-year-old, and [a child of] three, up to the age of six, goes out with his mother's eiruv. And just as for a one-year-old and a two-year-old it is speaking [of a case] without assigning an eiruv, so too for a four-year-old and a five-year-old it is speaking [of a case] where they did not establish an eiruv on his behalf. And even if we say "until" and not including "until," it is [still] a refutation of Rav Yehoshua, who answered that for a five-year-old one must assign [an eiruv] to him. [The Gemara concludes:] A conclusive refutation.

Rashi on Eruvin 82b:3:1.hebrew: לימא תהוי תיובתיה דרב אסי - דעד — ולא עד בכלל משמע, ואיהו אמר: אפילו בן שש:
Rashi on Eruvin 82b:3:1.english: Let us say that this is a refutation of Rav Asi - For "until" implies "up to, but not including," whereas he said: Even a six-year-old [is included].

Rashi on Eruvin 82b:4:1.hebrew: לימא תיהוי תיובתיה דר' ינאי ודריש לקיש - דמפרשי גבי סוכה: בר ארבע ובר חמשא קרי ליה ״אין צריך לאמו״, והכא תני ״יוצא בעירוב אמו״, ותניא לעיל דקטן שאינו צריך לאמו אינו יוצא בעירובה:
Rashi on Eruvin 82b:4:1.english: Let us say that this is a refutation of Rabbi Yannai and Reish Lakish - For they explain regarding [the laws of] sukkah [that a child of] four or five years old is called “not in need of his mother”; and here it teaches [that until the age of six he] “goes out with his mother’s eiruv,” and it was taught above that a minor who is not in need of his mother does not go out with her eiruv.

Rashi on Eruvin 82b:4:2.hebrew: הא דאיתיה לאבוה במתא - והתינוק נכנס ויוצא עמו, לא קרי ליה צריך לאמו מבן ד' ולמעלה, וברייתא — בדליתיה לאבוה במתא. ורב יהושע נמי לא מצי לשנויי הכי, דהא כי אותביניה לרב אסי לעיל, אם איתא דאית ליה לרב יהושע הא סברא, הכי הוה משני ליה לדרב אסי: בדליתיה לאבוה במתא, ונימא בדלא עירב שרי, ואשמעינן רבותא:
Rashi on Eruvin 82b:4:2.english: This [is a case] where his father is in town - And the child goes in and out with him, [so] he is not called [one who] "needs his mother" from [the age of] four and above. And the *baraita* [is referring to a case] where his father is not in town. And Rav Yehoshua could not answer in this manner either, for when we raised an objection against Rav Asi above, if it were so that Rav Yehoshua held this reasoning, this is how he would have answered on behalf of Rav Asi: [It is a case] where his father is not in town, and let him say that where [his father] did not make an *eiruv* [for him], it is permitted, and [thereby] teach us a novelty.

Rashi on Eruvin 82b:5:1.english: On their behalf - For their sake.

Rashi on Eruvin 82b:7:1.english: And their master established an eiruv for them - In a different direction.

Rashi on Eruvin 82b:8:1.english: A wife, in what way is she different - From a Hebrew servant and his adult son and daughter.

Rashi on Eruvin 82b:9:1.hebrew: הא סתמא - דאישתיקה, ולרוח אחרת נמי לא עירבה:
Rashi on Eruvin 82b:9:1.english: Whereas [in an] unspecified [case] - That she remained silent, and she also did not establish an eiruv in another direction.

Tosafot on Eruvin 82b:15:1.hebrew: וחצי חציה לפסול את הגוייה - והיינו שני ביצים. אומר ר"ת, דפסול גוייה גזירת קדמונים היתה, ולא מי"מ דבר דהאוכל אוכל ראשון ואוכל שני. תדע — דבפרק בתרא דיומא (דף פ:) סלקא דעתיה דהוי דאורייתא, ובעי למדרשיה מ"ולא תטמאו בהם ונטמתם בם", ובי"ח דבר היו בקיאין; ואם היתה דאורייתא, א"כ חסר להו! ועוד, דלשון "פסול גוייה" משמע דדוקא פסול הגוף, דנפסל גופו מלאכול בתרומה; וגזירה דהאוכל אוכל ראשון — פסול מגע הוא. אלא ודאי, פסול גוייה גזרו קודם י"ח דבר הרבה, ולא גזרו על מגעו שיפסל, אלא גופו מלאכול בתרומה. וגזרו על טומאת פנים אטו טומאת חוץ — שהרואה אוכל תרומה אחר שאכל אוכלין טמאין או שתה משקין טמאים, סבור שמותר ליגע בהן גם בחוץ תרומה טהורה, כמו שבתוך מעיו נוגעין זה בזה. ודווקא בשני ביצים; אבל בכביצה, אף על פי שראוי לטמא אחרים, לא גזרו — דא"א שלא ישאר קצת בין השינים והחניכין, או מתעכל קצת במעיו; וכיון דאפקוה מכביצה, אוקמוה אשני ביצים, שהוא חצי הסעודה דבית המנוגע (ולר' יוחנן בן ברוקה אביצה ומחצה). אבל במשקין טמאין שאינם מתעכלין ונכנס הכל במעיו, לא בעינן יותר מרביעית. אבל בי"ח דבר, דהאוכל אוכל ראשון, נזרו אפילו בכביצה, ושיפסול תרומה במגע, כדמפרש טעמא בפרק קמא דשבת (דף יד.) משום דזמנין דאוכל אוכלין טמאין כו', ואין להאריך כאן:
Tosafot on Eruvin 82b:15:1.english: "And half of its half to disqualify the body" - And that is [the volume of] two eggs. Rabbeinu Tam says that the disqualification of the body was an ancient decree, and not from the eighteen matters [enacted later, which include the decree concerning] one who eats food with first-degree impurity or food with second-degree impurity. Know [that this is so] — for in the final chapter of Yoma (80b), the Gemara initially thought that it was from the Torah, and sought to derive it from: "Neither shall you make yourselves unclean with them, that you should be defiled thereby" (Leviticus 11:43); and [the Sages] were well-versed in the eighteen matters, and if it were from the Torah, if so they would be missing [one of the eighteen decrees]! Furthermore, the phrase "disqualification of the body" implies specifically a disqualification of the person's body [itself], in that his body is disqualified from eating teruma; whereas the decree concerning one who eats food with first-degree impurity is a disqualification [imparted through] touch. Rather, it is certain that they decreed the disqualification of the body long before the eighteen matters, and they did not decree that his touch should disqualify [teruma], but only [disqualified] his body from eating teruma. And they decreed against internal impurity on account of external impurity — for one who sees [a priest] eating teruma after having eaten impure foods or drunk impure liquids might think that it is permitted to touch pure teruma to them externally as well, just as inside his innards they touch one another. And [this decree applied] specifically to two eggs; but for an egg's bulk, even though it is fit to impart impurity to other items [externally], they did not decree — as it is impossible that some [of the food] will not remain between the teeth and the gums, or be partially digested in his innards; and once they removed it from [the standard measure of] an egg's bulk, they established it at two eggs, which is half of the meal [relevant] to a leprous house (and according to Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, at an egg and a half). However, with impure liquids, which are not digested and enter entirely into his innards, we do not require more than a quarter-log. But among the eighteen matters, regarding [the decree of] one who eats food with first-degree impurity, they decreed [impurity] even with an egg's bulk, and that he disqualifies teruma through touch, as [the Gemara] explains the reason in the first chapter of Shabbat (14a): "Because at times one eats impure foods..." etc., and there is no need to elaborate here.

Tosafot on Eruvin 82b:3:1.hebrew: עד ועד בכלל - לא בעי לשנויי: "הא דאיתיה לאבוה במתא כו'", כדמשני בסמוך — דא"כ, הוי פליגי דרבי ינאי ור"ל אדרב אסי; והלכתא כרב אסי, דמייתי לה הש"ס בסוף פ' אע"פ (כחובות דף סה:):
Tosafot on Eruvin 82b:3:1.english: "Up to," and "up to" is inclusive - [The Gemara] did not wish to resolve [the objection against Rav Asi by answering]: "Here [is a case] where his father is in town, etc.," as it resolves immediately following, because if so, Rabbi Yannai and Reish Lakish would disagree with Rav Asi; and the halakha is in accordance with Rav Asi, as the Talmud cites it at the end of the chapter [entitled] Af Al Pi (Ketubot 65b).

Tosafot on Eruvin 82b:4:1.hebrew: הא דאיתיה לאבוה במתא כו' - לרב יהושע בריה דרב אידי לא הוי מצי לשנויי הכי, דהא לא מפליג בין איתיה לליתיה, מדלא משני הכי; וכן פירש בקונטרס:
Tosafot on Eruvin 82b:4:1.english: "Here, when his father is in town, etc." - For Rav Yehoshua the son of Rav Idi, [the Gemara] could not have answered like this, for he does not distinguish between [the father] being present and his not being present, as [is evident from the fact that] he did not answer like this [originally]. And so explained [Rashi in] the Kuntres.

Tosafot on Eruvin 82b:5:1.hebrew: מערב ע"י בנו ובתו הקטנים - ואור"י, דאף רבי יוחנן מודה הכא דקטן קטן ממש:
Tosafot on Eruvin 82b:5:1.english: "[A person] may establish an eiruv on behalf of his minor son or daughter" - And the Ri says that even Rabbi Yochanan concedes here that a minor is an actual minor [in age].

Tosafot on Eruvin 82b:6:1.hebrew: מפני שידן כידו - אעבדו ושפחתו קאי, כדאמרינן בריש הזורק בגיטין (דף עז:): דיד עבד קני ליה רביה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 82b:6:1.english: "Because their hand is like his hand" - [This] applies to his servant and his maidservant, as we say at the beginning of [the chapter] HaZorek in Gittin (77b), that the hand of a slave is acquired by his master.
